title: An ease from Allah is a gift. Accept it.
subtitle: Lightened prayer on the road, offered with mercy

row.title: we are safe now
sub: so is it still for us?

then: In the early years after the Hijrah, most travel was dangerous. Allah lifted blame for shortening the prayer on the road. Umar later wondered why it still applied in safe times, and the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}a charity Allah has given you, so accept His charity{/reward}.
now: You are exhausted on a long trip and feel guilty taking any ease. Or you are proud of always doing the hardest version of everything. {reward}Sometimes the humble thing is to receive what Allah gives.{/reward} His ease is love, not a lower grade.
old: Taking an ease Allah allows feels like doing less for Him.
new: Accepting His ease with gratitude is itself a way of honoring Him.
try: Next time Allah's law gives you an ease, take it and thank Him for it out loud.

title: Even facing danger, the prayer was not dropped.
subtitle: Guarding each other while standing before Allah
then: Abu Ayyash reported that at Usfan the enemy saw the Muslims at prayer and planned to strike at the next one, {trap}a prayer dearer to them than their own children{/trap}. These verses came down in between. The Prophet ﷺ led the prayer in shifts, {idea}each group guarding the other{/idea}.
now: Deadline night, a sick child, a twelve-hour shift on the ward. Your first thought is to skip the prayer. {idea}They kept it in front of an army.{/idea} And they did it by covering for each other. Who could you cover for so they can pray?
old: When life gets intense, prayer is the first thing to go.
new: Prayer stays, even in the hardest moments; we just help each other keep it.
try: At your busiest point today, take five minutes to pray on time, or cover for someone so they can.

title: Standing, sitting, lying down, keep remembering Him.
subtitle: Prayer has its times; remembrance has none
then: After the prayer in fear, Allah tells the believers to {idea}remember Him standing, sitting and lying down{/idea}, in every condition. When safe, they should pray fully and humbly. Ibn Abbas said prayer has {reward}a fixed time, just as Hajj does{/reward}.
now: You fold the prayer mat and pick up your phone, and Allah is out of your mind until the next adhan. The bus ride, the queue, the moment before sleep are all empty. {idea}The verse fills those gaps.{/idea} A quiet subhanallah fits in any posture.
old: I remember Allah when I pray.
new: Prayer is at its times, and remembrance fills everything in between.
try: Pick one daily wait, like the bus or the kettle, and make it your moment for dhikr today.

title: They hurt like you hurt. But you have hope.
subtitle: Same pain, different horizon
then: After battle the believers were wounded and tired. Allah told them not to weaken: {idea}they suffer as you suffer{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes the difference is that {reward}you hope from Allah for reward and help{/reward}, while they do not.
now: You are worn out from a long illness, a hard degree, a marriage you are working to save. Everyone struggles; you are not uniquely weak. {reward}What you carry that others may not is hope in Allah.{/reward} Let that be the thing that keeps you going.
old: I am struggling more than anyone, so maybe I should give up.
new: Everyone hurts, but I have hope in Allah, and that is reason enough to keep going.
try: When you feel like quitting today, say one dua that names what you are hoping Allah will give.

title: Do not become the advocate of the dishonest.
subtitle: Judging by truth, not by who argues best

row.conn: but if it is not his right

then: Allah sent the Book {idea}in truth, to judge by what Allah has shown{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ warned that he was only human and judged by what he heard: if someone won a case unfairly, {trap}it was a piece of the Fire{/trap}. Two disputing men wept and each gave up his claim.
now: Your cousin is in a dispute with a neighbor and the family expects you to back him. You know he is in the wrong. {trap}Arguing well for him does not make it right.{/trap} The verse asks you not to be the lawyer for something false.
old: Loyalty means always taking my people's side.
new: Loyalty never means defending what I know is dishonest.
try: If you are backing someone in an argument, ask yourself honestly whether they are in the right. Act on the answer.

title: After a call on justice, ask forgiveness.
subtitle: Turning to Allah after weighing others

row.title: I ask forgiveness
sub: for what I may have missed

then: Right after warning against siding with the deceitful, Allah says simply: {idea}seek forgiveness of Allah{/idea}. The command sits between instructions about judging fairly, a reminder that {reward}Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful{/reward}.
now: You mediated a fight between two friends and picked a side. You made a call at work that hurt someone's bonus. Even if you did your best, there may be things you missed. {idea}A quiet astaghfirullah after a hard call keeps you humble.{/idea}
old: If I tried to be fair, there is nothing to seek forgiveness for.
new: After any judgment on others, I turn to Allah for what I may have missed.
try: After the next decision you make about someone else today, say astaghfirullah three times.

title: Do not argue for those who betray themselves.
subtitle: Defending a deceiver hurts more than him
then: Continuing the passage, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ {idea}not to argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves{/idea}. Their deceit is against their own souls. And Allah does not love {trap}one who is a habitual, sinful betrayer{/trap}.
now: A colleague asks you to tell the manager he was with you all afternoon. A friend asks you to back up her story to her husband. {trap}Covering for deceit drags you into it.{/trap} You can stay kind without lending your voice.
old: Covering for a friend is a small kindness.
new: Arguing for someone's deceit harms them, harms me, and is not loved by Allah.
try: If someone asks you to back up a story that is not true, decline gently today and say why.

title: Hidden from people, never hidden from Allah.
subtitle: He is with them when they plot at night

row.title: no one will know
sub: as long as people do not

then: Ibn Kathir explains that they {trap}hid their wrongdoing from people so as not to be criticized{/trap}, yet exposed it to Allah, who knows their secrets. He is {idea}with them by His knowledge{/idea} when they spend the night in talk He does not accept.
now: You clear your browser history. You delete the message thread. You make sure your parents never find out. {idea}You worked so hard to hide it from people and forgot the One who was there.{/idea} He is also the One who forgives.
old: As long as nobody finds out, it is manageable.
new: I hide things from people but not from Allah, so He is the One I should face.
try: Think of one thing you hide from people. Tonight, talk to Allah about it honestly.

title: You defended them here. Who will defend them there?
subtitle: A verdict here is not a verdict there
then: Ibn Kathir explains that people might win a ruling in this world, since judges see only what is apparent. {trap}But on the Day of Resurrection, who will argue for them before Allah{/trap}, who knows the secret and what is more hidden? {idea}No one will speak for them.{/idea}
now: You got the refund you did not deserve. You won the family argument with a clever spin. Your lawyer got the better share of the inheritance. {idea}This is a reminder that the case is not closed.{/idea} There is still time to make it right.
old: If I won it fairly by the rules, it is mine.
new: Winning here does not settle anything before Allah, who knows what really happened.
try: Think of one thing you won that you were not entitled to. Take one step to give it back.

title: Whatever you did, ask, and you will find Him forgiving.
subtitle: The door stays open after any wrong
then: After the warnings to the deceitful, Allah opens the door wide. Ibn Abbas said whoever sins, minor or major, then asks forgiveness, will find Allah forgiving {reward}even if his sins were greater than the heavens, the earth and the mountains{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ spoke of {idea}wudu, two rakahs and asking forgiveness{/idea}.
now: It is two in the morning and you are lying awake over something you did years ago. You assume it is too late. {reward}The verse says: ask, and you will find Him.{/reward} Get up, make wudu, pray two rakahs, and tell Him.
old: What I did is too big to be forgiven.
new: No sin is bigger than Allah's forgiveness when I sincerely ask.
try: Tonight, make wudu, pray two rakahs, and ask Allah to forgive one specific thing.
